text: Francisco de las Carreras (1809–1870) was an Argentine lawyer, judge, and politician who served as the first President of the Supreme Court of Argentina from 1863 until his death in 1870. He completed his law studies at the University of Buenos Aires and entered politics during the administration of Juan Manuel de Rosas, serving as Minister of Finance for the Province of Buenos Aires in the 1850s. In January 1863, when President Bartolomé Mitre established the first Supreme Court, De las Carreras was appointed as a Minister. Following Valentín Alsina's refusal to assume the role of chief justice, De las Carreras was appointed chief justice on June 1, 1863, a position he held until his death. A street in Mar de Ajo is named in his honor, and in Buenos Aires, the largest city in Argentina, there is also a street named after him, located at Santiago Francisco de las Carreras.
